analysis:
The PR changes only one test file, provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests/KVCacheSSD/SSDCacheEpochStoreTests.swift. It removes the EpochOpenState actor and adds an onGCD helper (head lines 8-15). The test unloadedDeletionSerializesReopen (head lines 278-312) is rewritten to use DispatchSemaphores and GCD threads instead of Task.detached and a sleep-based check. The goal is to avoid cooperative-pool starvation while the process-wide epoch record lock is held. No production code, key handling, encryption, authorization or coordinator contract changes. No new attack surface.

Relevant threat T-041 (SSD prefix cache at-rest posture) is untouched in production behavior. The test still asserts that performUnloaded­DestructiveChange holds the initialization lock, that reopening waits for deletion to finish, and that the epoch and sequence are preserved (head lines 306-311).

Test-quality note, not a security finding: the reopen block calls deleted.wait(timeout: .now()) after the store constructor returns. That only passes if the constructor blocked until the mutation closure signaled. It is a weaker, timing-based serialization check (a 50ms sleep) but still detects a missing lock in the common case. A flaky pass or fail would not change the security posture.

No evidence of regression in epoch, rotation or wipe controls. The patch excerpt was truncated, but the full base and head texts were available and examined. Remaining gap: the production SSDCacheEpochStore implementation was not supplied, so this review checked only that the test's stated assertions are preserved, not the implementation.
